material_or_boundary: Stanfield, Denham and Tappenden; next Manning, continuing overleaf.
Manning closes; Anderson letter and postscript close; new Bath Oct. 13 letter starts “This is the 5th day of my residence in Bath”.
Continues the Bath letter, names “Mr. Bourdieu” in prose, closes to James Bourdieu Esqr London. Separate Thomas Day letter follows.
19 October letter to Richard Glover and sideways list of copies.

Bath, Oct. 22 through signature and address to James Bourdieu Esquire, London. An interlinear addition specifies the 20th instant. He encloses an address to Townshend and describes “forty Yards” in words. Margin supplies prose, with no code gloss.
Addressed to Thomas Townshend at Whitehall; new 23 October letter below it.
Thomas Day continuation and address.
Two Edward Bridgen letters. The number in a Long Acre postal address occurs in the first Bridgen letter.
Bridgen closes. Separate letter to the physician begins below dividing rule.
Brocklesby closes. Bath 30 October opens “I find myself indebted for your several ... Letters” and cites their dates, 22d, 25th, 28th.

Continues above the James Bourdieu Esqr London address, with postscript again addressed to James Bourdieu. Names Townshend and abbreviates him “Mr. T.”; mentions an anonymous paper. Margin lists packet copies.

Below close to Elias Vanderhorst, the Bourdieu letter is headed Dover 23d Nov. 1782 and closes to James Bourdieu, London. “23d” is the day; 20th is a letter date and 6 o'clock A.M./10 are times. The initials Mr J. B. Junr. have no adjacent number.
25 November letter to Edward Bridgen; sideways list records the 23 November letter dates.
Archibald Simpson letter and opening to a physician.
Dr Grant closes; fresh Bath 2d November letter references correspondence of the 30th ultimo and 31st. It quotes a letter in words.
Continues Bourdieu letter, twice spells out his surname in the opening lines and names Townshend. Closes to James Bourdieu Esqr London, followed by a separate letter.
Closes the letter to Townshend and then the separate William Manning letter; listing of copies on right.

Paris 30 November letter closes to James Bourdieu, London. “Should 44 wait on you” is followed by “him” and “the Gentleman”; no aligned expansion. Earlier lines recall an opinion given to the recipient and Mr Chollet in early May. Thomas Corbett letter below.
Mrs Oswald letter followed by new 3 December letter. The journey from Dover is repeated in words.
Edward Bridgen closes; separate 3 December Thomas Day letter follows. Common journey wording does not name the individual in Bourdieu's second paragraph.
Thomas Day closes and Edward Bridgen is named in the subsequent 4 December letter; sideways list of copies.
